The *Vimānavatthu* (Mansions of the Glorious) is a collection of verses from the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Canon. It describes various celestial mansions (*vimānas*) inhabited by beings who have attained rebirth there due to their meritorious deeds. **Purisavimāna** (The Mansion of the Man): This section features a series of stories concerning individuals who, through their virtuous actions, were reborn in magnificent celestial abodes. These narratives often contrast the humble circumstances of the person's previous life with the splendor of their new divine residence. **Pāyāsivagga** (Chapter on Pāyāsi): This chapter specifically concerns the story of Pāyāsi, a wealthy man known for his skepticism regarding the afterlife and the existence of heavenly realms. Despite his denial, he eventually performed acts of merit—such as giving alms to the Buddha and his disciples—which resulted in his rebirth in a glorious mansion. There, he encounters a group of deities who confirm the reality of the celestial worlds and the efficacy of karmic action. Through these encounters, Pāyāsi gains faith and attains the state of a stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*).
